content:
The Observatory forecasts that today's maximum outdoor temperature will reach 34 degrees, close to the 34.9 degrees recorded on the 'hottest Great Heat' in 2022, and about 4 degrees higher than last year's 'Great Heat'.

The Observatory has continued to issue the Very Hot Weather Warning, forecasting that today will be generally fine, but with showers in some areas from morning to noon, and extremely hot daytime temperatures. Additionally, a subtropical high-pressure ridge brings sunny conditions to Hong Kong, but the coast will also be affected by showers.

The heatwave triggered by the 'Great Heat' has made Hong Kong's streets feel as stifling as an oven, with a thermometer at Mong Kok MacPherson Playground recording a high of 40.8 degrees.

On past Great Heat days, the highest maximum temperature was 34.9 degrees in 2022, and the lowest was 22.2 degrees in 1965.

In addition, the highest average relative humidity and the highest total rainfall recorded on Great Heat in previous years were 96% and 195.1 millimetres in 1994, while the lowest average relative humidity was 70% in 1968.
